title: A proximity labeling protocol to probe proximity interactions in C. elegans
protocol: Synchronize and expand the C. elegans strains.
Transfer freshly starved L1 worms onto 150 mm NA22-seeded peptone-rich NGM plates.
Incubate the worms at 25°C until hermaphrodites are gravid but not yet starved.
Wash gravid hermaphrodites off of plates with M9 buffer.
Centrifuge the worms in conical tubes at 850×g for 1 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Add freshly prepared bleach (98 ml water, 6 ml 5N KOH, 12 ml sodium hypochlorite) and gently invert for approximately 7 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 850×g for 1 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash away the bleach by adding M9 buffer and gently inverting the tube for 5–15 s.
Repeat washing steps to completely wash away any residual bleach from the worms.
Plate approximately 100,000 embryos per 150 mm NA22-seeded peptone-rich NGM plate.
Do not allow the bleach treatment to last more than 8–10 min.
Wash worms off of the plates with M9 buffer.
Centrifuge worms in conical tubes at 850×g for 1 min.
Remove the supernatant and add fresh M9 buffer.
Repeat washing steps until supernatant is clear of bacteria (approximately five times).
Allow worms to settle by gravity for the final wash with M9 buffer.
Place worms on ice to expedite settling step.
Aliquot worms in desired amounts into Eppendorf tubes.
Remove as much M9 buffer supernatant as possible.
Freeze worm pellets in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C.
Transfer worm pellets from -80°C to ice.
Add 500 μL of high SDS RIPA lysis buffer for every 500 μL of worm pellet.
Once the pellet is thawed to 4°C, transfer the entire sample to a tube containing silica spheres.
Agitate at 6.5 m/s for 20 s pulses with 5-min breaks on ice.
Transfer the entire sample to clean tubes appropriate for sonication after agitation.
Sonicate at 18% at 5 s intervals with 5 s breaks for 50 s total in a 4°C water bath.
Add SDS-free RIPA buffer to achieve a final SDS concentration of 0.2%.
Gently rotate the lysate on a slow spinning wheel for 1 h at 4°C.
Transfer the samples to ultracentrifuge tubes and spin them at 4°C for 30 min at 51,000 RPM in a TLA-100.3 ultracentrifuge rotor.
Collect the liquid layer carefully (avoiding the lipid layer) and transfer it to a clean Eppendorf tube.
Take 2% of the liquid fraction and save it on ice as the "input" fraction.
Measure the protein concentration for each sample using the Pierce 660-nm Protein Assay.
Wash streptavidin-coated magnetic beads by adding 1 mL of RIPA lysis buffer.
Gently rotate the mixture on a spinning wheel for 5 minutes.
Pellet the beads with a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Repeat washing the beads two to three times in total.
Add an optimized volume of streptavidin-coated magnetic beads to 1 mg of protein for each sample.
Use 125 μL beads for achieving a ratio of 8 μg protein per 1 μL beads.
If samples are at unequal volumes, add additional RIPA lysis buffer to achieve similar volumes across samples.
Gently rotate the lysate on a slow spinning wheel at 4°C for 16 hours.
Store the rest of the lysate at -80°C.
Pellet the beads using a magnetic rack and remove the supernatant.
Set aside 2% of the supernatant as the "flow-through" fraction.
Wash each bead sample with buffers to remove nonspecific binders.
Keep the samples on ice between washes.
Add 1 mL of cold RIPA buffer, gently rotate at 20°C–23°C for 2 minutes, then pellet beads using a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of cold 1M KCl, gently rotate at 20°C–23°C for 2 minutes, then pellet beads using a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of cold 0.1 M Na2CO3, gently rotate at 20°C–23°C for 2 minutes, then pellet beads using a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of 2M urea, gently rotate at 20°C–23°C for 2 minutes, then pellet beads using a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of 4M urea, gently rotate at 20°C–23°C for 2 minutes, then pellet beads using a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of cold RIPA buffer, gently rotate at 20°C–23°C for 2 minutes, then pellet beads using a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Repeat step f. twice total.
Add 1 mL of cold PBS, gently rotate at 20°C–23°C for 2 minutes, then pellet beads using a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Repeat step h. five times total.
Dissolve urea in the Tris buffer and adjust pH with hydrochloric acid (HCl).
Prepare stock solutions of KCl, and Na2CO3 in water.
Add 3× sample buffer supplemented with 1:10 β-mercaptoethanol and 2 mM biotin to elute biotinylated proteins from beads more effectively.
Boil samples at 95°C for 10 min.
Vortex beads briefly then cool samples on ice.
Centrifuge the tubes briefly to bring down condensation.
Pellet the beads using a magnetic rack.
Collect eluate and place it on ice.
Add 4× sample buffer supplemented with β-mercaptoethanol to each input and flow-through fractions.
Dilute samples by mixing three parts sample with one part of 4× sample buffer.
Boil the diluted samples at 95°C for 10 minutes.
Place boiled samples back on ice.
Run equal volumes of input, flow-through, and biotinylation eluate samples for each genotype on one SDS polyacrylamide gel.
Transfer samples to a nitrocellulose membrane (0.4 μm).
Stain the membrane with Ponceau S solution to check protein transfer quality.
Remove Ponceau S stain by rinsing the membrane with water.
Block the membrane with 5% milk in 1× PBST for 30 minutes to 1 hour at 20°C–23°C or overnight at 4°C.
Incubate the membrane with anti-HA primary antibody (1:5000 in 1× PBST) for 1 hour at 20°C–23°C.
Wash the membrane three times with 1× PBST for 5 minutes each.
Incubate the membrane with a secondary antibody (1:5000, goat anti-rat IRDye 680RD, Licor) and streptavidin-IR Dye (1:5000, 800CW, Licor) in 1× PBST for 1 h at 20°C–23°C.
Wash the membrane three times with 1× PBST for 5 min each.
Image the blot on LI-COR Odyssey CLx or an equivalent technology.
